title: Requirements investigation
summary: Turn a request into a traceable brief before generating implementation tickets.

sections.label: Sequence
items: Read the request and relevant reviewed decisions from the sources your team uses.
Inspect pinned code/data revisions and existing verification.
Separate confirmed requirements, observed behavior, proposals, and unresolved questions.
Identify the affected data, components, interfaces and tests. Include only the parts that exist in this project.
Prepare acceptance scenarios and evidence links.

sections.label: Worked example
sections.text: In the reference-to-configuration case, the request is in Jira, reviewed decisions are in Confluence, and impact may include an ontology, SPARQL queries, services and a user interface. These illustrate the workflow. They are not required tools for other projects.

sections.label: Output
sections.text: A reviewed implementation brief: desired outcome, scope, source versions, affected components, acceptance criteria, uncertainties, and owner.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Every asserted requirement has supporting evidence or is explicitly proposed. Missing context remains visible rather than guessed.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Use the existing requirements mapping to turn evidence and unresolved questions into an implementation brief.
Trace each asserted requirement to a source or a visibly proposed decision.
Check acceptance scenarios against the agreed outcome and record missing constraints.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: GOV.UK discovery guidance connects problem definition, constraints and success measures to the decision about a next phase. This scoped source fact was checked on 15 October 2026. The guide's broader workflow and examples remain Atlas proposals, not demonstrated outcomes.

catalog.applicability: Use when a request must become a reviewed implementation brief before tickets are written. Every asserted requirement needs supporting evidence or an explicit proposal label, and missing context stays visible instead of being guessed.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
